purpose: An open-ended acceptance contract for automated original runtime and compiler lowering through O-core. This file states requirements, not a claim of installed, imported, executable, or cross-ISA support.

architectural_requirements.rule: Apply the referenced per-ISA acceptance matrix to every applicable mechanism and selected implementation. Missing 32-bit foundations remain required unfinished expansion work; 64-bit execution, target-object emission, and QEMU presence do not establish i686 or ARMv7 support. Require functional identity across every implemented O-core ISA under matched declared profiles, with dynamic backend inventory, original-reference and pairwise execution comparisons. Required unsupported or unavailable lanes remain RED/unmet; the listed targets are minimum obligations.

scope.architectural_objective: General automated import of external runtime and compiler implementations using existing implementation-language frontends and original build metadata, without a fixed language whitelist or interpreter-only ceiling.
scope.preserve_existing_work: Retain and extend all prior Rust, CPython, Node/V8, actual TypeScript, HTML, LaTeX, Java, C, D, Lua and provider investigations. Common Lisp, exact Chez Scheme and official Go are additional required families; no new entry replaces an unfinished implementation. OCaml is an additional required original compiler/runtime family and replaces none of these obligations.
scope.claim_rule: Report acceptance independently per original implementation, execution profile, artifact kind, and target. Family-wide or universal completion requires evidence for the actual claimed scope; one implementation or execution mode cannot establish every other one.

explicit_user_runtime_additions.scope: Complete original runtime/compiler lowering under every mandatory stage and applicable separate obligation; not registration or present support.

explicit_user_ocaml_and_all_isa_identity.functional_identity_scope: Every ISA in which O-core is implemented; dynamically inventory actual backends rather than treating existing profile lists as exhaustive.

required_before_selection: Exact upstream identity and source revision
Original build recipe and bootstrap requirements
Declared execution profile and required modules
candidate_policy.existing_recipe_rule: Audit existing recipes and evidence before selecting or changing a candidate. File existence, command catalog presence, or a prepared recipe does not prove build health or successful lowering.

evidence_required: Pinned original upstream source identity and hashes
Complete source and resource manifest for the declared profile
Audited original build and bootstrap recipe
Recorded source patches with purpose and semantic impact
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Use the original implementation. Infrastructure patches must be disclosed and reviewed; replacing implementation logic with a manual O-core rewrite, generated facade, reduced teaching implementation, or different engine cannot establish this implementation's acceptance.

evidence_required: olangc-owned recipe and frontend invocations
Full command, environment, toolchain, target, and build-input provenance
Complete expected-versus-captured translation-unit and generated-source inventory
Build-time tools and dependencies distinguished from shipped runtime dependencies
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: olangc owns original source acquisition or resolution, build recipe, frontend invocation, capture, and failure reporting. Capture all required original compilation units, including generated sources and target-specific units; inventory-only success is insufficient.

evidence_required: Per-unit import results matched to the expected complete source inventory
Complete required functions, globals, constants, initializers, relocations, modules, and compiler helpers
Exact unsupported constructs and affected units
Mapping from original implementation units to emitted O-core-owned modules
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Every required unit and construct for the declared profile must lower through O-core with original observable semantics. Reject unsupported constructs explicitly. No silently omitted units, unresolved native stubs, interpreted unchanged foreign IR, or external original-engine executable may substitute for lowering.

evidence_required: Independent O-core verifier invocation and actual exit status for each required module
Verifier identity and module hashes
Diagnostics and negative outcomes retained
Module-consistency verification
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: A successful importer or emitter must not certify itself by implication. Run the applicable independent verifier on every emitted module, then verify final linkage and the complete artifact at artifact construction; parse success, a feature census, or an evidence filename is insufficient.

evidence_required: Complete recursive declared dependency and resource graph
Resolved functions, globals, initializers, relocations, libraries, helpers, and native module references
Provider implementation identity, provenance, ABI, target, and qualification
Explicit required platform interfaces and external effects
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Every required native implementation reference resolves within the included compiled dependency closure. Declare platform interfaces explicitly; an allowlisted unresolved native implementation, host-installed runtime, or supplied executable is not a complete compiled closure.

evidence_required: Target-specific calling conventions, data layout, and relocation support
Required varargs, aggregates, vectors, floating point, atomics, TLS, exceptions, and unwind features
Initializer and finalizer ordering
Resolved final link map and symbol table
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Validate every ABI feature actually used by the original implementation and its closure. Reduced argument tests or one successful translation unit do not establish complete ABI support.

evidence_required: Single olangc-owned workflow from declared source recipe to artifact
Artifact manifest and hashes
Independent whole-program linkage, module-consistency, and complete-artifact verification
Compiled original runtime or compiler plus complete native dependency closure
Included .O program, foreign scripts, resources, execution profile, realization bindings, linkage, and provenance
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: The artifact must be a complete whole program for its declared profile. OIR orchestration and O-core MIR retain distinct invariants and explicit runtime/operation interfaces. An OIR artifact may include compiled native modules, but every native module reference must resolve in its included dependency closure. Supplied original-engine executables and orchestration-only plans do not establish original-engine compilation.

evidence_required: Actual artifact execution command and environment
Exit status and retained stdout/stderr
Representative upstream conformance and regression workloads for the declared profile
Observable-behavior comparison with the original implementation
Clean-environment dependency-closure check
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Exercise the compiled original implementation through the shipped .O and foreign-script path. Foreign scripts may be interpreted by the O-core-compiled original language runtime. Artifact construction alone does not establish executable support. An IR artifact must receive its required native lowering and execution qualification before an execution claim is made.

evidence_required: Separate x86_64, AArch64, and RV64GC artifact and execution evidence
Exact ISA, OS, ABI, architecture features, and execution profile
Native hardware versus emulator identity clearly identified
Observable-semantics comparison and declared treatment of nondeterminism
Unsupported target-specific constructs and interfaces retained
Frozen dynamic inventory of every implemented O-core ISA/backend and complete expected-versus-executed mechanism/profile matrix; retain all minimum required targets even when foundations are missing
Unchanged-original-reference versus owned execution on each ISA plus pairwise matched owned executions across every implemented ISA, with exact workload/input/profile/artifact/result identities

Declared deterministic, floating-point, memory/concurrency and nondeterministic observation models; retained raw results, semantic mismatches, missing executions and meaningful cross-ISA negative controls
mandatory_acceptance_stages.acceptance: Qualify equivalence per execution profile on all required targets. Successful host execution, cross-emission, static verification, or a runtime's name does not imply cross-ISA equivalence or purity. Preserve required external effects and specify environment-dependent equivalence explicitly. Every implemented O-core ISA is required: enumerate actual source/build/runtime backends and qualify functional identity against the unchanged original reference and between matched owned executions. Never normalize away mismatches, silently omit an ISA, or use compilation/static checks as semantic equivalence. Follow the referenced all-implemented-ISA contract; unresolved profile conflicts and gaps remain RED/unmet.

compiler_implementation_import.requirement: Compile the original compiler implementation and its complete declared closure through O-core under the mandatory acceptance stages. Bootstrap tools are recorded separately and cannot stand in for the final compiled compiler.

compiler_generated_program_routing.requirement: Have olangc automatically route programs produced by the original compiler through O-core import, verification, ABI adaptation, dependency resolution, linking, artifact construction, and actual execution. Importing a compiler implementation alone does not satisfy this capability.

jit_generated_code.requirement: Keep JIT implementations in scope. Declare and verify a concrete generated-code capture, O-core lowering, relocation, publication, execution, and invalidation path with original runtime semantics. An interpreter profile may be qualified separately but cannot establish JIT support or permanently remove JIT work from scope.

replayability.requirement: Track replayability, external effects, and admission independently from lowering. Do not infer purity or determinism from the source language or runtime identity.

Rust standard library and required compiler support libraries

Bootstrap and generated-source capture
Compiler-produced Rust programs routed through O-core
Panics, unwind or declared abort profile, allocation, TLS, atomics, and target runtime behavior
language_families.non_substitute: A small Rust crate, reduced probe, or manually rewritten library is evidence only for that probe and cannot replace rustc or the required standard library.

candidate_upstreams: CPython
specific_obligations: Complete original interpreter/compiler implementation for the declared profile
Required standard-library modules, extension-module providers, encodings, imports, and resources
Reference semantics, exceptions, initialization, dynamic loading, and threading profile
Actual Python scripts carried by the olangc artifact

QuickJS as an additional engine profile
V8 including an explicitly tracked JIT scope
specific_obligations: Preserve the existing Node.js/V8 backend's original-engine profile and audit its pinned upstream producer and complete host/module/provider closure
An additional QuickJS profile must not silently replace the existing Node.js/V8 profile or establish its acceptance
Original selected engine and complete declared module/provider closure
JavaScript parsing, execution, exceptions, modules, and required host interfaces
Interpreter and JIT profiles assessed separately

candidate_upstreams: Upstream TypeScript compiler implementation resolved by pinned revision and producer audit
An independently admitted original JavaScript engine for generated JavaScript

Lower the complete original compiler body and its dependencies through the appropriate implementation-language frontend and O-core path, including the native/Go implementation where selected by the audited upstream revision
A historical JavaScript tsc profile may be declared and qualified separately but cannot establish lowering of a different current native compiler implementation
Complete compiler libraries, module resolution, declaration inputs, and resources
Compiler-generated JavaScript routes through the admitted selected original O-core-compiled JavaScript engine or a separately verified native O-core compilation path
Compiler-body lowering, TypeScript compile diagnostics, and generated-program execution have separate evidence
language_families.non_substitute: A handwritten transpiler, syntax stripper, or supplied JavaScript-engine executable does not establish upstream TypeScript support.

candidate_upstreams: A genuine upstream HTML DOM and rendering engine selected after source/build audit
specific_obligations: Original parser, DOM, layout, and rendering implementation for the declared profile
Required CSS, JavaScript integration, encoding, resource loading, graphics, font, and platform providers
Actual DOM and rendering workloads with documented observable comparison
Documented browser or headless execution profile and its complete resources
language_families.non_substitute: The built-in text formatter, string interpolation, an HTML generator, or markup passthrough does not establish DOM or rendering-engine lowering.

candidate_upstreams: An original TeX-family engine
Upstream LaTeX format and required packages and fonts
specific_obligations: Original TeX engine implementation lowered through O-core
Complete declared format, macro, package, font, encoding, hyphenation, and resource closure
Original build and format-generation steps captured
Actual document compilation and output behavior qualified per execution profile
language_families.non_substitute: A LaTeX-like formatter, rendered fixture, or host TeX executable is not evidence of original TeX-engine lowering.

specific_obligations: Original JVM and compiler implementation plus required class-library and native-provider closure

specific_obligations: Complete original compiler implementation and required runtime/provider closure

dmd

candidate_upstreams: SBCL
ECL
CLISP
Clozure Common Lisp (CCL)
specific_obligations: Pin and preserve the actual original Common Lisp implementation, compiler/runtime, bootstrap inputs, generated images, libraries, native code and complete declared providers. Existing adapter fallback selection is not implementation equivalence.
Capture original implementation-language and architecture-specific producers under olangc ownership; supplied bootstrap executables/images are build inputs, not final lowered-runtime evidence.
Preserve reader/macros, packages, lexical and dynamic binding, CLOS/generic functions, conditions/restarts/non-local exits, numeric behavior, GC, FFI and declared thread behavior.

reference_workloads: Pinned upstream conformance/regression suite plus macro/package/closure/dynamic-binding/condition/restart and numeric cases
GC/root liveness, object identity, finalization, FFI/callbacks and declared thread/effect cases

Silently selected different Common Lisp engine
Opaque supplied executable or precompiled original-engine image used as lowering proof
Unlowered compiler-produced/native-generated code or ABI/platform mismatch

candidate_upstreams: Chez Scheme original compiler and runtime
specific_obligations: Require Chez Scheme itself, pinned original compiler/runtime/boot-image and library sources, generated bootstrap products, native primitives, providers and FFI closure.
Preserve proper tail calls, continuations, multiple values, dynamic-wind, exceptions, numeric behavior, library loading, GC roots and declared thread/foreign-call behavior.
Capture and lower original Scheme/C/assembly producers and complete target-specific sources through registered verified interfaces; unsupported producers stay unmet.
Separate compiler-body lowering, compiled Scheme output, runtime-generated code, publication/invalidation and image/boot reconstruction obligations.

reference_workloads: Pinned upstream Chez tests and complete declared libraries/boot resources
Deep proper-tail-call, captured/reentered continuation, multiple-value, dynamic-wind, exception and GC/root-liveness cases
Original versus owned compiler/runtime/FFI behavior on each required ISA
negative_controls: Another Scheme engine or authored Scheme subset substituted for Chez
Unlowered generated code or opaque host Chez executable/image

language_families.non_substitute: Generic Scheme support, another Scheme implementation, an unchanged implementation-IR interpreter or launching a supplied Chez executable is not original Chez runtime lowering.

candidate_upstreams: Official Go compiler, Go runtime and required standard library
specific_obligations: Use pinned original official Go compiler/runtime/required standard-library and internal-package sources, bootstrap tools and declared generated resources.

Register and verify actual Go, assembly and cgo producers where used; preserve target-specific assembly, ABI/stack conventions, stack maps, GC barriers, atomics and full recursive package/provider closure.
Preserve goroutine scheduling and stack growth, channels/synchronization, interfaces/reflection, maps, GC/root liveness, panic/defer/recover, finalizers and declared cgo/platform effects.

Compile original compiler implementation and route programs it generates through O-core as distinct capabilities; Go-host compilation/execution outside the owned path does not close either requirement.

reference_workloads: Pinned upstream runtime/compiler/standard-library tests for the complete declared profile
Goroutine/channel synchronization, growing stacks with live roots, GC barriers/stack maps, atomics and interface/reflection/map cases
Panic/defer/recover and FFI/cgo callbacks where declared; native original versus owned programs on each required ISA
negative_controls: Missing Go/assembly/internal-package/compiler-helper unit, relocation, initializer or provider
Dropped stack map/GC barrier/ABI metadata or changed scheduler/stack semantics
Toy Go-like runtime, substituted scheduler/GC, external go run or supplied executable as lowering proof
Compiler body accepted while generated programs bypass O-core or wrong target ABI is silently reused

language_families.non_substitute: A Go-like interpreter, reduced runtime, alternative engine silently replacing official Go, discarded assembly, external Go compiler/runtime process or supplied native programs cannot establish complete official Go lowering.

candidate_upstreams: Original official OCaml compiler, bytecode runtime, native runtime and standard library
specific_obligations: Pin unchanged original OCaml compiler/runtime/standard-library sources, selected upstream revision, license, bootstrap tools and bytecode/native bootstrap products, generated sources, native assembly, build metadata, target configuration and complete recursive providers/resources. Candidate naming does not select or qualify an upstream revision.

Drive full original implementation-language and architecture-specific units through olangc-owned registered producers, complete O-core import, independent verification, ABI/link/initializer resolution and complete native/verified O-core IR/OIR artifact construction. Preserve all cold functions, globals, relocations and original runtime/compiler behavior; unsupported producers and units remain RED/unmet.

Qualify original bytecode VM/runtime lowering and execution of OCaml bytecode programs separately from original compiler-body lowering, native/runtime compiler lowering and compiler-generated native-program routing through O-core. Bytecode execution by the O-core-compiled original VM is permitted; interpreting unchanged imported implementation IR is not lowering the VM or compiler.

Preserve value/tag and integer-width representations, heap layouts, precise GC roots and stack maps, allocation/safepoints/barriers, closures and partial application, proper tail calls, exceptions, effects/continuations, modules/functors/standard libraries, FFI/callbacks and original data/marshalling/unmarshalling behavior under the declared profile.

Preserve systhreads, domains, synchronization/atomics, memory model, GC/finalizer interaction and target-specific native assembly/platform interfaces. Required effects/domain-capable and other execution lanes cannot be closed by selecting an older or reduced profile that lacks them; retain actual upstream/profile applicability and missing capabilities explicitly.

Keep bytecode compilation/output, native compilation/output, dynamic linking and any applicable runtime-generated code/publication/invalidation paths distinct. Bind complete owned artifacts and unchanged-reference behavior to each actual ISA/profile, including every implemented O-core ISA and the minimum required expansion profiles.

reference_workloads: Pinned upstream compiler/runtime/stdlib conformance and regression workloads, with full required bytecode and native build inventories and separately identified original implementation, compiler and generated-program artifacts

Tagged values, int/nativeint/float representations, GC/root liveness and relocation, minor/major allocation and barriers, custom blocks/finalizers, closures/partial application/tail calls and exceptions under the declared semantic profile
Effects/continuation capture and resumption, modules/functors, FFI and callbacks, original marshalled/unmarshalled data and declared resource/module loading

Systhreads/domains, atomics and GC/synchronization interactions; native assembly and platform behavior; unchanged upstream versus owned execution plus pairwise matched executions on every implemented O-core ISA
negative_controls: Missing required original bytecode/native/compiler/stdlib/assembly unit, cold function/global, initializer/relocation, provider, generated resource or boot artifact
Wrong tag/heap/data layout, lost GC root/stack map/barrier, broken closure/tail call/exception/effect/continuation or unmarshalling behavior
Bytecode VM success substituted for native compiler/output qualification, compiler body accepted while generated programs bypass O-core, or reduced profile used to claim all execution modes
Host OCaml executable/image, alternative implementation, toy runtime, manually rewritten engine or unchanged implementation-IR interpreter used as original-runtime lowering evidence
ABI/platform/assembly/atomic/domain mismatch, an omitted implemented ISA, missing reference/pairwise comparison, or an altered cross-ISA observable incorrectly accepted

language_families.non_substitute: An OCaml-like interpreter, alternate implementation, supplied host compiler/runtime executable, partial bytecode-only profile, handwritten runtime or unchanged implementation-IR interpreter cannot establish complete original OCaml compiler/runtime support.

provider_workstream.acceptance: Apply the same original-source, capture, import, independent-verification, provenance, ABI, linkage, closure, execution, and target requirements to required implementation providers. Separate explicit platform interfaces from bundled implementations, record every unresolved dependency, and preserve existing provider work.

evidence_record_requirements.completion_rule: Use qualified_for_declared_scope only after every mandatory stage and applicable separate capability obligation has evidence for that exact implementation/profile/artifact/target claim. Retain failures and commands; distinguish observed output from expectations.
evidence_record_requirements.metrics_rule: Unit counts and feature percentages may describe progress but never certify completeness. One missing required unit, dependency, ABI feature, resource, or module reference blocks the corresponding complete-support claim.
evidence_record_requirements.test_rule: Use meaningful upstream and end-to-end workloads. Reduced probes diagnose blockers and remain labeled as probes. They cannot replace the original engine/compiler or its complete declared dependency closure.
evidence_record_requirements.independent_review_rule: Before qualifying a milestone, retain a separate reviewer assessment of changed lowering/code generation, generated-runtime source inclusion, complete required-unit inventories, and semantic oracles, with findings and resolution. Reviewer approval does not replace actual verification/execution evidence. Use a separate reviewer agent when available.
evidence_record_requirements.all_implemented_isa_identity_rule: Retain the dynamically derived implemented-ISA inventory, complete applicable mechanism/profile matrix, per-ISA original-reference comparisons and pairwise matched owned executions. List minimum targets separately from implemented status; missing/unsupported/unexecuted lanes remain RED/unmet and cannot disappear from the expected set. Coverage must fail closed when a backend is added without applicable target/runner/oracle coverage. Require exact defined deterministic observations and the same defined concurrency/nondeterministic allowed-trace semantics; matching a few schedules is bounded evidence.

prohibited_completion_evidence: Embedding or launching a supplied original-engine executable
Manually reimplementing a language runtime in O-core
Generating O-core text from a polyglot block without lowering the original runtime
Interpreting unchanged imported foreign IR as proof of native runtime lowering
Silently omitting failed original units or replacing them with semantic stubs
Using toy crates, reduced engines, or handwritten transpilers as substitutes for named original implementations
Counting captured units or feature percentages as complete runtime/compiler support
Treating command, path, recipe, or artifact presence as proof of functioning execution
Treating compiler implementation import as compiler-generated program routing
Treating host-only execution or static cross-emission as cross-ISA semantic qualification
One ISA or a fixed target whitelist used as universal functional-identity proof while an implemented O-core ISA is omitted
Compilation-only, object-emission-only or zero-execution comparisons presented as all-ISA semantic equivalence
Floating-point, memory, concurrency or nondeterministic mismatches normalized away or silently filtered

A new implemented backend omitted from CI/acceptance target, guarded runner or independent oracle coverage; unsupported features excluded to turn RED into green; a few matching schedules presented as all-trace identity

primary_runtime_lowering_test_priority.property: O-core must lower arbitrary original language-runtime implementations through reusable producer/build/import interfaces
primary_runtime_lowering_test_priority.primary_tests: End-to-end original-source runtime lowering, complete verification/closure/artifacts and declared-profile behavior
primary_runtime_lowering_test_priority.required_profile_missing_prerequisites_o: unmet acceptance, retain failures, no silent skip/zero-case pass
